title: Generic Methods & Method-Level Type Inference
summary: Define generic methods independent of class-level types: <T> returnType methodName(T arg), type inference, and static generic utility methods.
learningObjectives: Master the generic method syntax: declaring <T> immediately before the return type
Define static generic utility methods inside both generic and non-generic classes
Analyze javac type inference algorithms and when explicit type witnesses (<Type>) are required
Avoid the dangerous type variable shadowing pitfall between class-level and method-level parameters
expectedOutcomes: Ability to build high-performance, reusable utility libraries like java.util.Collections
Mastery of method-level type argument inference and compile-time resolution

activities.title: Practical Context: Universal Luggage Baggage Scale at Airport Check-In

analogy.headline: Practical Context: Universal Luggage Baggage Scale at Airport Check-In
analogy.story:
At an international airport check-in desk, the baggage scale does not care what kind of bag is placed on it: a hardshell suitcase, a golf club duffle bag, a musical cello case, or a cardboard box. The scale mechanism (the method) is parameterized by the incoming object.

It accepts item T, reads its mass, stamps a baggage tag of type Tag<T>, and hands it back. The check-in desk building itself (the class) does not need to be a 'SuitcaseBuilding' or 'CelloBuilding'. The method independently adapts to whatever specific baggage type is presented in that single transaction.
analogy.keyTakeaway: A generic method introduces its own type parameter scoped strictly to that single method execution, independent of whether the enclosing class is generic.

activities.title: Generic Method Syntax, Type Witnesses & Shadowing Traps

keyTakeaways: Generic methods declare formal type parameters BEFORE the return type: public static <T> void swap(T[] arr, int i, int j)
Generic methods can exist inside non-generic classes, enabling standalone utility libraries
The Java compiler infers type arguments automatically from invocation parameters and target assignment types
Type witnesses (Collections.<String>emptyList()) supply explicit type arguments when inference context is ambiguous
A method-level <T> shadows a class-level <T>, creating confusing compilation diagnostics

activities.title: Generic Array Reversal Utility
activities.description: Trace a static generic array reversal method operating across diverse reference types.

steps.description: Define <T> immediately before void. This introduces type parameter T scoped strictly to reverse().
Two-pointer swap algorithm. Variable temp is of type T, safely holding elements without casting.
Compiler automatically infers T as String on tokens and T as Double on values.

questions.question: Where must the formal type parameter section <T> be placed in a generic method declaration?
options: After the method parameter list: public void doSomething(int x)<T>

questions.question: What is the syntax for supplying an explicit type witness when calling a static generic method 'create()' on class Factory?
questions.explanation: An explicit type witness is placed between the dot and the method name: Factory.<String>create().

activities.title: Senior Engineer Interview: Static Methods & Generic Classes

qaList.question: Why can a static method inside a generic class 'Holder<T>' declare its own '<T> static void process(T val)', and does this method-level 'T' have any relationship to the class-level 'T'?
qaList.answer: A static method cannot access the class-level type parameter 'T' because static methods belong to the loaded class archetype and are shared across all instances (e.g., Holder<String> and Holder<Integer> share the exact same static method). However, a static method can introduce its OWN independent type parameter by declaring '<T>'. Even though both use the letter 'T', they are completely distinct and independent type variables: the method-level 'T' shadows the class-level 'T'. To eliminate developer confusion and warnings, best practice is to rename the method-level type parameter to '<E>' or '<U>'.

activities.title: Self-Evaluation Checklist
checklist: I know the exact placement of <T> before the return type in generic methods
I understand how the Java compiler infers method type arguments automatically
I know how and when to provide an explicit type witness: Class.<Type>method()
I understand the difference between class-level and method-level type parameter scopes

practiceProblems.title: Generic Element Frequency Counter
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a generic static method countOccurrences(T[] array, T target) that returns the number of elements in the array that are equal to the target using Objects.equals().

practiceProblems.title: Generic Dual-List Zipper
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a generic static method zip(List<A> listA, List<B> listB) that pairs corresponding elements from two lists into a List of Pairs until the shorter list is exhausted.

practiceProblems.title: Generic Maximum of Three Elements
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a generic static method maxOfThree(T a, T b, T c) that determines and returns the greatest of three values of any type T that implements Comparable<T>.

practiceProblems.title: Generic Array to Unique Set Converter
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a generic static method arrayToSet(T[] array) that converts any array of reference types into a java.util.HashSet<T>, preserving unique elements.

practiceProblems.title: Generic First Non-Null Coalescer
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a generic static method coalesce(T... values) that inspects a varargs sequence of elements and returns the first non-null element, or null if all elements are null.
